children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast were steady to stronger on Monday, reflecting exporter demand amid a run of US soybean sales to China.

The US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 114,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China, the fourth sales announcement to China in as many business days, and another 261,000 tons sold to undisclosed destinations.
Separately, the USDA reported export inspections of US soybeans in the week to October 15 at 2,001,750 tons, topping a range of trade expectations for 1,200,000 to 1,600,000 tons.
Nearly half of the soybean total was exported from the Gulf, USDA data showed.
Export inspections for corn were 672,475 tons, well below trade expectations ranging from 1,100,000 to 1,350,000 tons.
US harvest progress has favored soybeans. The USDA said the soybean harvest was 64% complete as of Sunday, up from 46% the previous week, but behind the five-year average of 65%.
The US corn harvest was 44% finished, up from 33% previously and behind the five-year average of 52%.

At the Gulf, CIF soybean barges loaded in the last half of October were bid at 95 cents over Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) November soybean (SX26) futures, unchanged from Friday. November bean barges were bid at 109 cents over futures, up a penny from Friday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in first-half November held steady at around 117 cents over futures.
For corn, CIF corn barges loaded in last-half October were bid at 83 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures. November corn barges were bid at 89 cents over futures, down 2 cents from Friday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first half of November were around 101 cents over CBOT December futures, unchanged from Friday.
